title: Tests overwrite or delete environment keys and clean up by deleting them instead of restoring the previous value; Vitest runs many files in one worker process, so values leak between files and, before the rails, the real .env values were deleted for later files

evidence.note: sets MEV_* keys in beforeEach and deletes them in afterEach without saving the previous values
deletes EXIT_DUST_THRESHOLD_BPS and EXIT_ROUTINE_MAX_FAILURES in beforeEach
sets EXIT_ROUTINE_MAX_FAILURES = 5 inside a case; never restored
sets WATCHDOG_BUDGET_MS and deletes it afterwards
before the rails the real .env was loaded into process.env, so a delete removed the operator value for the rest of the worker
the worker loops over its files and only resets modules between them; process.env persists

evidence.ref: node scratchpad tools/envscan.js over the TESTU snapshot
evidence.note: per-file counts of env assignments, deletes and save/restore idioms

sibling_sites_checked: envscan.js over all 84 files: save-and-restore idioms (SAVED_ENV loops) in bot/deliberateBuy*, bot/noDoubleBuyReconcile, exitEngine/exitInclusionLadder, exitEngine/noDoubleSellReconcile, mevStrategies/inclusionReconciliation (correct). Delete-only or no cleanup: the files listed here plus the Task 2 files added to this finding.
severity_rationale: S3: order-dependent test results (a case can pass only because an earlier file in the same worker set or deleted a key); no direct capital effect, and the rails now replace the real values with sentinels.
recommendation: Phase 28: use vi.stubEnv with unstubEnvs (or save and restore the previous value) for every env change.
affected_cases: every case in the listed files that sets or deletes a key
escaped_regression: A change that makes the exit engine read EXIT_ROUTINE_MAX_FAILURES at import instead of per call passes or fails depending on which file ran earlier in the worker (failedExitBalanceTruth.test.ts:289 leaves 5 behind), so the suite result depends on file order rather than on the code.
